title: Prakrama 2, Sarga 4. Immersion in the Heavenly River
html:
Shuklambara's ecstasy; the Lord's dances and play; the parable of the conjurer; instructions to Mukunda and Murari; the service of Srivasa and Rama; the Lord bathes in the Ganga after hearing Krishna's name reviled

Verse 1

तत्र शुक्लाम्बरो नाम द्विजो रोदिति नित्यशः।
पतित्वा दण्डवद्भूमौ वदन्नेवं मुहुर्मुहुः॥१॥

tatra śuklāmbaro nāma dvijo roditi nityaśaḥ|
patitvā daṇḍavadbhūmau vadannevaṁ muhurmuhuḥ||1||

tatra — there; shuklambarah nama — named Shuklambara; dvijah — the brahmana; roditi — weeps; nityashah — constantly; patitva — falling; dandavat — like a stick; bhumau — to the ground; vadan — saying; evam — thus; muhur muhuh — again and again.

1The brahmana named Shuklambara wept there constantly; falling to the ground like a stick, he said again and again:

Verse 2

नवद्वीपस्तु मथुरा कृता तात त्वयाधुना।
इति संविलपन्भूमौ रोदिति प्रेमविह्वलः॥२॥

navadvīpastu mathurā kṛtā tāta tvayādhunā|
iti saṁvilapanbhūmau roditi premavihvalaḥ||2||

navadvipah — Navadvipa; tu — indeed; mathura — into Mathura; krita — has been made; tata — O dear one; tvaya — by You; adhuna — now; iti — thus; samvilapan — lamenting; bhumau — on the ground; roditi — weeps; prema-vihvalah — overwhelmed by love.

2"Now You have made Navadvipa into Mathura1, O dear one!" — and, lamenting thus, he wept on the ground, overwhelmed by love.

Verse 3

वयस्यांसे विनिक्षिप्तकरो नृत्यति कर्हिचित्।
क्वचिद्रोमाञ्चिततनुः कल्पते परमः पुमान्॥३॥

vayasyāṁse vinikṣiptakaro nṛtyati karhicit|
kvacidromāñcitatanuḥ kalpate paramaḥ pumān||3||

vayasya-amse — on a friend's shoulder; vinikshipta-karah — with His hand placed; nrityati — dances; karhichit — sometimes; kvachit — sometimes; romanchita-tanuh — His body's hair standing on end; kalpate — appears; paramah — the Supreme; puman — Person.

3Sometimes the Supreme Person danced with His hand on a friend's shoulder, and sometimes the hair of His body stood on end.

Verse 4

क्वचिदीश्वरभावेन भृत्येभ्यः प्रददौ वरान्।
एवं नानाविधाकारैर्नृत्यँल्लोकानशिक्षयत्॥४॥

kvacidīśvarabhāvena bhṛtyebhyaḥ pradadau varān|
evaṁ nānāvidhākārairnṛtya~llokānaśikṣayat||4||

kvachit — sometimes; ishvara-bhavena — in the mood of the Lord; bhrityebhyah — to His servants; pradadau — gave; varan — boons; evam — thus; nana-vidha-akaraih — in manifold forms; nrityan — dancing; lokan — the people; ashikshayat — taught.

4Sometimes, in the mood of the Lord, He gave boons to His servants. Thus, dancing in manifold forms, He taught the people.

Verse 5

कदाचित्स्वजनस्कन्धमारुह्य हर्षयन्विभुः।
स्वजनान्क्रीडति प्रीतः क्षणदायां कृतक्षणः॥५॥

kadācitsvajanaskandhamāruhya harṣayanvibhuḥ|
svajanānkrīḍati prītaḥ kṣaṇadāyāṁ kṛtakṣaṇaḥ||5||

kadachit — once; svajana-skandham — onto the shoulders of His own people; aruhya — having climbed; harshayan — delighting; vibhuh — the Almighty; svajanan — His own people; kridati — plays; pritah — pleased; kshanadayam — at night; krita-kshanah — making a festival.

5Once at night, making a festival, the Almighty, well pleased, climbed onto the shoulders of His own people and played with them, delighting them.

Verse 6

अथापरदिने भूमावुपविश्यानुनादयन्।
करतालैर्दिशः प्रोचे पश्य शैलूषचेष्टितम्॥६॥

athāparadine bhūmāvupaviśyānunādayan|
karatālairdiśaḥ proce paśya śailūṣaceṣṭitam||6||

atha — then; apara-dine — on another day; bhumau — on the ground; upavishya — sitting; anunadayan — making resound; kara-talaih — with hand-claps; dishah — the quarters; proche — said; pashya — look; shailusha-cheshtitam — the conjurer's act.

6On another day He sat on the ground and, making all the quarters resound with the clapping of His hands, said: "Look, here is a conjurer's trick!

Verse 7

पश्य पश्याद्भुतं बीजं भूमौ संरोपितं मया।
पश्य पश्याङ्कुरो जातो निमिषेण तरुः पुनः॥७॥

paśya paśyādbhutaṁ bījaṁ bhūmau saṁropitaṁ mayā|
paśya paśyāṅkuro jāto nimiṣeṇa taruḥ punaḥ||7||

pashya pashya — look, look; adbhutam — wondrous; bijam — seed; bhumau — in the ground; samropitam — planted; maya — by Me; pashya pashya — look, look; ankurah — a sprout; jatah — has appeared; nimishena — in the twinkling of an eye; taruh — a tree; punah — then.

7Look, look: I have planted a wondrous seed in the ground! Look, look: a sprout has come up — and in the twinkling of an eye it has become a tree!

Verse 8

जातं पश्यास्य पुष्पौघं पश्य पश्य फलं पुनः।
जातं पश्य फलं पक्वं तस्य संग्रहणं पुनः॥८॥

jātaṁ paśyāsya puṣpaughaṁ paśya paśya phalaṁ punaḥ|
jātaṁ paśya phalaṁ pakvaṁ tasya saṁgrahaṇaṁ punaḥ||8||

jatam — come forth; pashya — look; asya — on it; pushpa-augham — a mass of flowers; pashya pashya — look, look; phalam — fruit; punah — then; jatam — has appeared; pashya — look; phalam — the fruit; pakvam — ripe; tasya — its; sangrahanam — gathering; punah — then.

8Look: a mass of flowers has blossomed on it! Look, look: now there is fruit! Look: the fruit is ripe — and now it is being gathered!

Verse 9

फलं वृक्षोऽपि नास्त्येव क्षणान्मायाकृतं यतः।
प्रान्तरे तु कृतं ह्येवं न किञ्चिदपि लभ्यते॥९॥

phalaṁ vṛkṣo'pi nāstyeva kṣaṇānmāyākṛtaṁ yataḥ|
prāntare tu kṛtaṁ hyevaṁ na kiñcidapi labhyate||9||

phalam — fruit; vrikshah — tree; api — also; na asti eva — there is none at all; kshanat — in a moment; maya-kritam — made by maya; yatah — since; prantare — in a deserted place; tu — but; kritam — done; hi — indeed; evam — thus; na kinchit api — nothing at all; labhyate — is gained.

9Yet there is no fruit and no tree at all, for it is all made in a moment by maya; and if such a thing is shown in a deserted place, nothing is gained.

Verse 10

ईश्वरस्याग्रतः कृत्वा धनं विपुलमश्नुते।
एवं मायाकृतं कर्म सर्वं चेदमनर्थकम्॥१०॥

īśvarasyāgrataḥ kṛtvā dhanaṁ vipulamaśnute|
evaṁ māyākṛtaṁ karma sarvaṁ cedamanarthakam||10||

ishvarasya — of a lord; agratah — before; kritva — having done; dhanam — wealth; vipulam — abundant; ashnute — gains; evam — thus; maya-kritam — done by maya; karma — work; sarvam — all; cha — and; idam — this; anarthakam — fruitless.

10But by showing it before a lord, (the conjurer) gains abundant wealth. So too every work done by maya is fruitless in itself;

Verse 11

ईश्वरार्थं कृतं ह्येतत्सर्वं सार्थकतामियात्।
तस्मादीश्वरसेवार्थं सर्वं कर्माचरेत्सुधीः॥११॥

īśvarārthaṁ kṛtaṁ hyetatsarvaṁ sārthakatāmiyāt|
tasmādīśvarasevārthaṁ sarvaṁ karmācaretsudhīḥ||11||

ishvara-artham — for the Lord's sake; kritam — done; hi — but; etat — this; sarvam — all; sarthakatam — fruitfulness; iyat — would attain; tasmat — therefore; ishvara-seva-artham — for the Lord's service; sarvam — every; karma — work; acharet — should perform; sudhih — the wise.

11but all that is done for the Lord's sake will bear fruit. Therefore let the wise perform every work for the service of the Lord."

Verse 12

ततः प्रोवाच भगवान्मुकुन्दाम्बष्ठमग्रतः।
स्थितं प्रेक्ष्य त्वया किं नु ब्रह्मविद्या निजोच्यते॥१२॥

tataḥ provāca bhagavānmukundāmbaṣṭhamagrataḥ|
sthitaṁ prekṣya tvayā kiṁ nu brahmavidyā nijocyate||12||

tatah — then; provacha — said; bhagavan — Bhagavan; mukunda-ambashtham — Mukunda the Ambashtha; agratah — before (Him); sthitam — standing; prekshya — seeing; tvaya — by you; kim nu — is it that; brahma-vidya — knowledge of Brahman; nija — your own; uchyate — is expounded.

12Then, seeing Mukunda the Ambashtha2 standing before Him, Bhagavan said: "Can it be that you are expounding a knowledge of Brahman of your own?"

Verse 13

इत्युक्त्वा स पपाठेदं श्लोकं स्वयमरिन्दमः।
श्रीरामनाममाहात्म्यं गूढवेदार्थसंग्रहम्॥१३॥

ityuktvā sa papāṭhedaṁ ślokaṁ svayamarindamaḥ|
śrīrāmanāmamāhātmyaṁ gūḍhavedārthasaṁgraham||13||

iti — thus; uktva — having said; sah — He; papatha — recited; idam — this; shlokam — verse; svayam — Himself; arin-damah — the Subduer of foes; shri-rama-nama-mahatmyam — on the glory of the name of Sri Rama; gudha-veda-artha-sangraham — containing the hidden meaning of the Vedas.

13Having said this, the Subduer of foes Himself recited a verse on the glory of the name of Sri Rama, containing the hidden meaning of the Vedas:

Verse 14

रमन्ते योगिनोऽनन्ते सत्यानन्दचिदात्मनि।
इति रामपदेनासौ परं ब्रह्माभिधीयते॥१४॥

ramante yogino'nante satyānandacidātmani|
iti rāmapadenāsau paraṁ brahmābhidhīyate||14||

ramante — take delight; yoginah — the yogis; anante — in the Infinite; satya-ananda-chit-atmani — whose nature is truth, bliss and consciousness; iti — therefore; rama-padena — by the word "Rama"; asau — that; param brahma — the Supreme Brahman; abhidhiyate — is designated.

14"The yogis take delight in the Infinite, whose nature is truth, bliss and consciousness; therefore the Supreme Brahman is designated by the word 'Rama'3."

Verse 15

पुनः प्रोक्तं भगवता तं वैद्यमनुशासता।
चतुर्भुजस्य यद्ध्यानं तद्वरं परिकीर्तितम्॥१५॥

punaḥ proktaṁ bhagavatā taṁ vaidyamanuśāsatā|
caturbhujasya yaddhyānaṁ tadvaraṁ parikīrtitam||15||

punah — again; proktam — it was said; bhagavata — by Bhagavan; tam — that; vaidyam — vaidya; anushasata — instructing; chatur-bhujasya — of the Four-armed; yat — which; dhyanam — meditation; tat — that; varam — best; parikirtitam — is declared.

15And again Bhagavan, instructing that vaidya, said: "You hold that meditation on the Four-armed is the best,

Verse 16

द्विभुजस्य तु यद्ध्यानं तन्न्यूनमिति ते मतम्।
परमेश्वरभेदेन केवलं दुःखमेव हि॥१६॥

dvibhujasya tu yaddhyānaṁ tannyūnamiti te matam|
parameśvarabhedena kevalaṁ duḥkhameva hi||16||

dvi-bhujasya — of the Two-armed; tu — but; yat — which; dhyanam — meditation; tat — that; nyunam — inferior; iti — thus; te — your; matam — opinion; parameshvara-bhedena — by making distinctions in the Supreme Lord; kevalam — only; duhkham — misery; eva hi — indeed.

16and that meditation on the Two-armed is inferior. But making distinctions in the Supreme Lord brings nothing but misery.

Verse 17

यद्यात्मनो हितं वेत्सि तदा यत्नपुरःसरम्।
द्विभुजध्यानमेव त्वं कुरु सर्वफलप्रदम्॥१७॥

yadyātmano hitaṁ vetsi tadā yatnapuraḥsaram|
dvibhujadhyānameva tvaṁ kuru sarvaphalapradam||17||

yadi — if; atmanah — for yourself; hitam — the good; vetsi — you know; tada — then; yatna-purahsaram — with diligence; dvi-bhuja-dhyanam — meditation on the Two-armed; eva — alone; tvam — you; kuru — practise; sarva-phala-pradam — granting all fruits.

17If you know what is good for you, then diligently meditate on the Two-armed alone: it grants all fruits."

Verse 18

ततः प्रोवाच तं देवं मुकुन्दो नम्रकन्धरः।
गौराङ्गचरणाम्भोजमधुपो गायकोत्तमः॥१८॥

tataḥ provāca taṁ devaṁ mukundo namrakandharaḥ|
gaurāṅgacaraṇāmbhojamadhupo gāyakottamaḥ||18||

tatah — then; provacha — said; tam — to that; devam — Lord; mukundah — Mukunda; namra-kandharah — with bowed neck; gauranga-charana-ambhoja-madhupah — a bee at the lotus feet of Gauranga; gayaka-uttamah — the best of singers.

18Then Mukunda, the best of singers, a bee at the lotus feet of Gauranga, bowing his neck, said to the Lord:

Verse 19

स्नातं मया सुरनदीपयसि प्रकामं
श्रीवैष्णवाङ्घ्रिरजसाङ्गमलङ्कृतं च।
त्वत्पादपद्मवरछत्रममुं मयाद्य
मूर्ध्नि प्रयच्छ कुरु दास्यपदेऽभिषेकम्॥१९॥

snātaṁ mayā suranadīpayasi prakāmaṁ
śrīvaiṣṇavāṅghrirajasāṅgamalaṅkṛtaṁ ca|
tvatpādapadmavarachatramamuṁ mayādya
mūrdhni prayaccha kuru dāsyapade'bhiṣekam||19||

snatam — has been bathed; maya — by me; sura-nadi-payasi — in the water of the river of the gods; prakamam — to my heart's content; shri-vaishnava-anghri-rajasa — with the dust of the feet of the Vaishnavas; angam — body; alankritam — adorned; cha — and; tvat-pada-padma-vara-chhatram — the excellent umbrella of Your lotus feet; amum — this; maya — for me; adya — today; murdhni — on the head; prayachchha — place; kuru — perform; dasya-pade — into the office of servant; abhishekam — consecration.

19"I have bathed to my heart's content in the waters of the river of the gods, and my body is adorned with the dust of the feet of the holy Vaishnavas; now place on my head this excellent umbrella of Your lotus feet — consecrate me into the office of Your servant4."

Verse 20

एवं निशम्य तद्वाक्यं तस्य मूर्ध्नि पदाम्बुजम्।
दत्तवान्भगवांस्तुष्टः सहर्षोऽभूत्तदैव सः॥२०॥

evaṁ niśamya tadvākyaṁ tasya mūrdhni padāmbujam|
dattavānbhagavāṁstuṣṭaḥ saharṣo'bhūttadaiva saḥ||20||

evam — thus; nishamya — having heard; tat-vakyam — his words; tasya — his; murdhni — on the head; pada-ambujam — His lotus foot; dattavan — placed; bhagavan — Bhagavan; tushtah — pleased; sa-harshah — joyful; abhut — became; tada eva — at once; sah — he.

20Having heard these words, Bhagavan, well pleased, placed His lotus foot on his head, and at once he was filled with joy;

Verse 21

रोमाञ्चिततनुर्धीमानश्रुपूर्णविलोचनः।
ततो मुरारिं प्रोवाच भगवानम्बुजेक्षणः॥२१॥

romāñcitatanurdhīmānaśrupūrṇavilocanaḥ|
tato murāriṁ provāca bhagavānambujekṣaṇaḥ||21||

romanchita-tanuh — the hair of his body on end; dhiman — the wise; ashru-purna-vilochanah — his eyes full of tears; tatah — then; murarim — to Murari; provacha — said; bhagavan — Bhagavan; ambuja-ikshanah — the lotus-eyed.

21the hair of the wise man's body stood on end and his eyes filled with tears. Then the lotus-eyed Bhagavan said to Murari:

Verse 22

कथं त्वं कृतवान्वैद्य गीतमध्यात्मतत्परम्।
जीविते यदि वाञ्छास्ति प्रेम्णि वा ते हरेः स्पृहा॥२२॥

kathaṁ tvaṁ kṛtavānvaidya gītamadhyātmatatparam|
jīvite yadi vāñchāsti premṇi vā te hareḥ spṛhā||22||

katham — how is it that; tvam — you; kritavan — composed; vaidya — O vaidya; gitam — a song; adhyatma-tatparam — devoted to the doctrine of the Self; jivite — for life; yadi — if; vanchha — desire; asti — there is; premni — for love; va — or; te — your; hareh — of Hari; spriha — longing.

22"How is it that you, vaidya, have composed a song on the doctrine of the Self? If you desire life, or if you long for love of Hari,

Verse 23

तदा गीतं परित्यज्य कुरु श्लोकं हरेः स्वयम्।
तच्छ्रुत्वा प्राह तं देवं विनयेन भिषक्सुधीः॥२३॥

tadā gītaṁ parityajya kuru ślokaṁ hareḥ svayam|
tacchrutvā prāha taṁ devaṁ vinayena bhiṣaksudhīḥ||23||

tada — then; gitam — the song; parityajya — giving up; kuru — compose; shlokam — a verse; hareh — about Hari; svayam — yourself; tat — that; shrutva — having heard; praha — said; tam — to that; devam — Lord; vinayena — humbly; bhishak — the physician; sudhih — wise.

23then give up that song and compose a verse about Hari yourself." Hearing this, the wise physician humbly answered the Lord:

Verse 24

श्रीमन्नारायणो नाम गुप्तः स्नेहार्णवं गुरुम्।
यथा तवावतारोऽयं वक्तुमर्हति साम्प्रतम्॥२४॥

śrīmannārāyaṇo nāma guptaḥ snehārṇavaṁ gurum|
yathā tavāvatāro'yaṁ vaktumarhati sāmpratam||24||

shriman narayanah nama — He who is called Sriman Narayana; guptah — hidden; sneha-arnavam — the ocean of affection; gurum — the guru; yatha — so that; tava — Your; avatarah — descent; ayam — this; vaktum arhati — may be told; sampratam — now.

24"Sriman Narayana, now hidden, is the guru, the ocean of affection5. So that this descent of Yours may now be told,

Verse 25

तथाज्ञां कुरु देवेश तच्छ्रुत्वा सस्मिताननः।
प्राह तं भगवानस्य तथैव सम्भविष्यति॥२५॥

tathājñāṁ kuru deveśa tacchrutvā sasmitānanaḥ|
prāha taṁ bhagavānasya tathaiva sambhaviṣyati||25||

tatha — such; ajnam — a command; kuru — give; deva-isha — O Lord of the gods; tat — that; shrutva — having heard; sa-smita-ananah — with a smiling face; praha — said; tam — to him; bhagavan — Bhagavan; asya — for him; tatha eva — just so; sambhavishyati — it will be.

25give such a command, O Lord of the gods." Hearing this, Bhagavan said to him with a smile: "So it will be for him.

Verse 26

यद्वदिष्यत्यसौ वैद्यस्तत्सुसत्यं भविष्यति।
एतच्छ्रुत्वा हरेर्वाक्यं नोचे किञ्चिद्भयात्तु सः॥२६॥

yadvadiṣyatyasau vaidyastatsusatyaṁ bhaviṣyati|
etacchrutvā harervākyaṁ noce kiñcidbhayāttu saḥ||26||

yat — what; vadishyati — will say; asau — this; vaidyah — vaidya; tat — that; susatyam — perfectly true; bhavishyati — will be; etat — this; shrutva — having heard; hareh — of Hari; vakyam — the word; na uche — did not say; kinchit — anything; bhayat — out of awe; tu — and; sah — he.

26Whatever this vaidya says will be the truest truth." Hearing these words of Hari, he said nothing more, out of awe.

Verse 27

मुरारिर्मुमुदे तत्र श्रीमच्छ्रीवासपण्डितः।
शुद्धस्वाचारनिरतो हरिसेवापरायणः॥२७॥

murārirmumude tatra śrīmacchrīvāsapaṇḍitaḥ|
śuddhasvācāranirato harisevāparāyaṇaḥ||27||

murarih — Murari; mumude — rejoiced; tatra — then; shrimach-chhrivasa-panditah — Sriman Srivasa Pandita; shuddha-sva-achara-niratah — devoted to pure, good conduct; hari-seva-parayanah — dedicated to the service of Hari.

27Murari rejoiced then. And Sriman Srivasa Pandita, devoted to pure and good conduct and dedicated to the service of Hari,

Verse 28

Notes

  1. Mathura is the place of Krishna's birth and pastimes.
  2. Mukunda Datta, the celebrated kirtana singer; Ambashtha is the caste of the vaidyas (physicians).
  3. A verse of the Padma Purana, also quoted in the Chaitanya-charitamrita (Madhya 9.29).
  4. Literally, "perform the abhisheka (consecration) into the office of servant," as at a royal coronation.
  5. Verse 24 is syntactically unclear; the translation is tentative. The Lord's reply (vv. 25–26) is understood as His blessing on Murari to tell of His descent — that is, to compose this poem.
  6. Kapila is the sage, a descent of Vishnu, the teacher of the Sankhya doctrine.
  7. The heavenly river is the Ganga.
